gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured power draw or case temperature for any 4K dash cam under $200: Chuck McCoy (DashCamTalk forum) measured the Viofo A119M Pro at 4.0-4.2 W and 63-80 °C, and EricSan measured the Vantrue S1 Pro Max at 4.9 W front alone and 8.7 W with a 4K rear camera; nor does any result say the A119M Pro's 62 Mbps arrived only with firmware V1.2_20260409 (37 Mbps before).
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages. Product Bible (productbible.com/blog/best-dash-cams-under-200) carries no measured figure at all. RoadGearLab (roadgearlab.com/best-4k-dash-cam/) already quotes DashCamTalk bitrates for the A119M Pro (about 62 Mbps) and 70mai A810S (about 29 front, 10 rear) and says 'We have not tested these cameras ourselves', so the bitrate half of this angle is not new for those two cameras. RoadGearLab has no watts, no measured case temperature, no firmware condition on the 62 Mbps, and no measured figure for the Vantrue S1 Pro Max or Vantrue E1 Pro. Car and Driver's under-$170 test could not be opened (fetch blocked), so it was not compared.
decides: Confirms the Viofo A119M Pro as the front-only pick: it has the highest measured bitrate (62 Mbps against 29.4-32 for the others at the same 3840x2160, 30 fps), the lowest measured driving draw (4.0-4.2 W) and DashCamTalk's highest score of the group (7.8). Two cautions: the 62 Mbps needs firmware V1.2_20260409 or later, and Viofo's own store charges $209.99 today, so it is under $200 only at other sellers (DashCamTalk's tracker shows Amazon at $132.99). For front plus rear, the measurements do not separate our Vantrue S1 Pro Max from the 70mai A810S on front bitrate (31.9 against 29.4 Mb/s), but DashCamTalk scores it lower (6.8 against 7.7) and EricSan's 8.7 W with a rear camera was taken on the 4K+4K kit, not the $199.99 4K+2.5K kit. One finding threatens a row of ours: Vortex Radar reports the multi-camera Botslab G980H uses a 5 MP SmartSens SC501AI and calls its 2160p25 mode 'fake 4K'; I did not establish whether the 4K+2K dual kit shares that sensor, so check that before listing it as a 3840x2160 row.
